description: Device bridge (RFC 0083, workstream 0003 leg 3): grants the loaded self-hosted instance — a runtime-chosen, non-local origin — IPC access to exactly one app-defined command, `bridge_invoke`, and nothing else. Deliberately separate from the `default` capability, which stays local-only (no `remote` field) and keeps its broader core:default/store:default grant scoped to the bundled onboarding page only, per this repo's 'remote instance content must never get Tauri IPC access' rule. `bridge_invoke`'s `notifications.native` and `camera.photo` actions do exactly what a plugin could already do by calling the standard Web Notifications API or a browser file input in a browser tab, just backed by real native delivery (`tauri-plugin-notification`'s `NotificationExt`, `tauri-plugin-dialog`'s `DialogExt`). `biometrics.confirm` (macOS/Windows only, epic task 17.10) is narrower rather than equivalent: no browser-tab API grants this — it calls `LocalAuthentication.framework`/`Windows.Security.Credentials.UI` directly — but it is scoped to a local presence confirmation only, never a session or platform-auth grant (see `src/biometrics/mod.rs`'s doc comment), so it still cannot do anything with broader consequence than the two actions beside it. All three plugins' own JS-invokable commands are never granted to any origin, local or remote; only this crate's Rust-side calls into them run.
